hypotheses.justification: The variable command `variable {K : Type} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]` makes `[DecidableEq K]` an argument of the theorem: it is instance-implicit, it mentions only `K`, and `K` is an argument. There is no `omit` in the file. Nothing in the statement needs it: `W.ψ n`, `W.ΨSq n`, `Polynomial.evalEval`, `Polynomial.eval` and `W.toAffine.Equation` are all defined for a commutative ring and do not need decidable equality. The proof does not use it either. It rewrites with `map_pow`, `Affine.CoordinateRing.mk_ψ` and `Affine.CoordinateRing.mk_Ψ_sq`, which are stated for a commutative ring. It then applies `AdjoinRoot.mk_eq_mk`, a general commutative-ring lemma, followed by ring-level rewrites (`evalEval_sub`, `evalEval_pow`, `evalEval_C`, `evalEval_mul`, `zero_mul`, `sub_eq_zero`). There are no `if`s and no `Finset` operations on `K` that would need `DecidableEq K`. So the same proof compiles under `omit [DecidableEq K] in`. Degenerate cases are not an issue: the identity holds for every field `K`, every `n` and every point `(x, y)` on the curve, whether or not equality on `K` is decidable.
